reEndorsement: This re-pin is an integrity refresh over a mechanism correction, not a new grant. It writes one packet digest and two T02 receipt digest lines so the tree's recorded hashes match its bytes. The correction itself removes a false refusal: OBX-AUTH-R1-P2-SOLO-001 declared that the eight P1 files were absent when it was written, and the verifier read that declaration as a standing claim about the tree, so P1 doing exactly the work OBX-AUTH-R1-P1-SOLO-001 authorizes made the P2 record look stale and blocked every P1 branch. Removing a false refusal is not widening authority, and none was widened: no record's allowedPaths, allowedEffects, forbiddenEffects, expiry, invalidators or acceptedRisk changed, because no record changed at all. The P2 activation precondition still stands in the record, in the amendment and in the module: no OBX-P210 child ticket may start before the P1 phase merges, and the gate now enforces that against the two things that would actually show P2 starting early - an OBX-P210 child ticket in the program manifest, or a path only the P2 record authorizes appearing before the merge. Two properties are recorded on purpose. First, this record is not in the release-1 phase module's activationWriteSet constant, by design: the module lists the seventeen files an activation pull request may write, docs/audits/ is excluded from the packet digest, and a re-pin record that named itself in its own governed write set would be circular. It is therefore unpinned by the phase records and stands on the verification evidence above. Second, the delivered phase-only rule is narrower than the literal criterion it answers, and the reason is recorded in reReviewMethod rather than left for a reader to discover.
